title: Start here and study calendar
angle: A front chapter that she acts on today: what to do before booking, which route to take through each chapter, and a relative Day 1 to Day 19 calendar with two variants and readiness gates. It starts from calendar-preview.md (2026-10-04) and changes only what has a stated reason. Every exam rule is a linked exam-* fact of chapter 01; every study time and threshold is the book's own plan.

contents: One sentence: the book prepares her for AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate (SAA-C03), linked with a display of exam-name-and-code. Do not claim that SAA-C03 is the current version or that no new version is coming: request fr-0014 is open.
One sentence with two links: the exam has [65 questions](exam-question-count) in [130 minutes](exam-duration-minutes).

The four domains with their weights as four links of exam-domain-weights (displays '30% of scored content' and so on), in a 2-column plain table (Domain | Share of scored content) or one list. Then: her diagnostic of 2026-09-18 was weakest in Secure (45%) <!-- no-fact: plan -->, and Secure is also the largest domain, so the calendar puts security first.

The parts of the book in 3 to 4 short list items: 00 to 02 start; 03 to 43 services and patterns; 44 to 49 and 52 review sheets; 50 and 51 the book's own mocks. Name the web version and the Anki export only as things that come with the book; no dates.

Keep the preview's three routes and minutes (SPEC templates.*.minutes still give the same values): Fast = read 1-fast.md, about 20 minutes for a deep chapter and 12 for a medium chapter. Pass = Fast, then the core questions in 5-quiz.md, then only the 2-deep.md subsections that the wrong answers point to (they are marked for the Pass route), then one spoken answer from 4-say.md: about 50 minutes for a deep chapter (65 for IAM, VPC, S3 and EC2) and 22 for a medium chapter. Full = every file with the tasks in 3-do.md: about 2 hours 15 minutes for a deep chapter and 1 hour for a medium chapter; mostly for after she passes.
Format: a 3-column plain table (Route | What you do | Deep / medium time) or three bold-led list items; the preview used a list.
One sentence: the real minutes of each chapter stand in its front matter and on its first line in the web version; when they differ from this table, use the chapter's value.

Grounding: role orient is heuristic. Time units are exempt only in a sentence without an exam_fact_words word (exam, retake, reschedule, score, scored, result, voucher, ESL, accommodation, Pearson). Write 'after you pass', not 'after the exam', in a sentence that has minutes.

A chapter is a folder of short files: 1-fast.md (the short version, read first), 2-deep.md (How it works, numbers, the decision record, FAQ quick-fire), 3-do.md (tasks in AWS CloudShell), 4-say.md (spoken answers), 5-quiz.md (questions), sources.md. One short list.

The devices she meets first, one line each: Predict (guess before reading; not scored), Signals and traps (the 'But not if' column stops keyword matching), Changed recently (old value, new value, what older questions can assume), Stop and answer at the end of each How-it-works subsection, Go deeper blocks for edge cases.

The reading rule in one sentence, with a link: each exam question asks you to select the responses that [best complete the statement or answer the question](exam-select-best-response-instruction), so find the constraint in the stem (cost, operational overhead, security) before you read the options.

One sentence that introduces Callvale from STARTUP.md A1 line 1 (a fictional startup that sells a call-intelligence service; Ana and Ben founded it). No numbers. Not a Startup example callout (front chapters carry none).

The four spoken moves as a 2-column plain table, copied from the preview: 1 Answer | 'The short answer is ...'; 2 How | 'It works like this ...'; 3 Watch | 'The thing to watch is ...'; 4 You | 'In your case ...', then ask one question back. Then the practice rule from the preview: 10 minutes every day, standing; read the model answer aloud first, then answer without the text against a 90-second timer.
Exam trap callout start-here-trap-new-feature-examinable (see traps), placed after the Changed recently line; ends with <!-- trap: start-here-trap-new-feature-examinable -->.

A numbered list of 3 steps. Step 1, bold lead 'Request ESL +30 first.': link [ESL +30](exam-esl-accommodation) and [30-minute exam extension](exam-esl-accommodation) in the first sentence; the 'once' claim uses the new display 'only needs to be requested once' (request fr-0017; until it is filled, write <!-- needs-display: exam-esl-accommodation "only needs to be requested once" --> and do not use the display 'requested once, prior to registering for an exam', because 'prior to' is a banned word). Path, copied from the preview: sign in to [aws.training/Certification](exam-certification-account) > Go to your Account > Request Exam Accommodations > Request Accommodation > Accommodation Type: ESL +30 MINUTES > Create.

Step 2, bold lead 'Then book Day 19.': register after step 1 is done, for Day 19 of Plan A counted from your Day 1; choose a test center or online proctoring (link exam-testing-options, display 'Pearson VUE' or 'Online proctoring is available for all AWS Certification exams'). Do not state reschedule numbers here; calendar.md#readiness-gates has them.

Step 3, bold lead 'Take the free official practice set.': the AWS Certification Official Practice Question Sets are [20-question sets](exam-official-practice-question-sets) on AWS Skill Builder; take the SAA-C03 set before you study, as your baseline, and write each miss into mistakes.md. Name the Skill Builder subscription only without a price (request fr-0009 is open), or leave it out.
Exam trap callout start-here-trap-esl-after-booking after the list; ends with <!-- trap: start-here-trap-esl-after-booking -->.
Exactly 3 prompts, each with a <details><summary>Answer</summary> reveal; the role is strict, so a reveal that states a hard fact links it.
Recap 1. What do you request before you book the exam? Answer: [ESL +30](exam-esl-accommodation), in your AWS Certification Account.
Recap 2. Which route do you take for most chapters before the exam? Answer: Pass: Fast, the core questions, the subsections your misses point to, one spoken answer.
Recap 3. What are the four moves of a spoken answer? Answer: Answer, How, Watch, You, with their starters.
Each prompt asks only for something stated above it in 1-fast.md (U4).

contents: About 70 words of use: Day 1 is the first day you study; the days run on without a gap, so Days 3 and 4 are light days. Start with Plan A. Plan B (a later exam) and Plan C (an earlier exam) are variants; the gates say when to switch. Each row gives the minutes and the work; a chapter is named by its number, title and route. On Day 1, request ESL +30 before booking. With ESL +30 you get [130 minutes](exam-duration-minutes) plus a [30-minute exam extension](exam-esl-accommodation); train at 130 and sit at 160 (the 160 stands in a sentence of its own, without an exam word, as arithmetic of the two linked facts).

Then a paragraph that starts with the bold lead '**Changed since the preview.**' and a short list of at most 4 items, at most 80 words in all (see changed_since_preview below). 'since' is a warn word; the label is the name the RULINGS use, so keep it.

plan-a.plan_region: <!-- plan:start id=a --> / <!-- plan:end -->, filled by sync from data/plan.json; exactly 19 rows
contents: One line before the region: Plan A is the full plan: 19 days, about 41 hours, or 38 without mock 5 (see Gate 1).

After the region, the mock method from the preview: a mock is one full Tutorials Dojo practice exam in timed mode, in one quiet two-hour block, then about 1 hour of review with the cause codes of mistakes.md. Pace: 2 minutes or less per question, then your flagged questions (link [Flag for Review](exam-timer-and-review) if the sentence names the exam's own button). Answer every question: an unanswered question is [scored as incorrect](exam-no-guessing-penalty) and there is [no penalty for guessing](exam-no-guessing-penalty). The unscored questions are [not identified on the exam](exam-unscored-questions-not-identified), so give every question the same care. Only first attempts in timed mode count toward a gate.

Optional, not in the total (from the preview): the tasks in 3-do.md (do Task 0, the budget alert, which is the first Try of chapter 02, before any other task); the Pass route for the Fast chapters of Days 11 and 13; the light chapters 20, 30 and 36; 49 Speaking pack; the book's own mocks 50 and 51; Anki.

plan-b.plan_region: <!-- plan:start id=b --> / <!-- plan:end -->; 10 rows (Day 1, then Days 15 to 23); rows_max of a plan table is 19, so Plan B lists Day 1 and the days from Day 15 on
contents: When: Gate 1 or Gate 2 says move. Plan B keeps Days 1 to 17 of Plan A and moves the exam to Day 23 (or Day 24: then add one light day before the review sheets). A repair day follows mock 5 and mock 6. About 47 hours.

The cost, from the preview, made relative: no retake fits before a deadline that is close, and the result can come late: final results arrive [within five business days](exam-results-timing) after the exam, and most exams show [no pass or fail on screen](exam-no-result-on-screen). Count five business days from Day 23 before you choose it; if that passes your deadline, Plan B does not fit. Check Plan B against your other deadlines in that week (the preview named slides and a panel week).

When: you need an earlier exam, for example to keep room for one retake before a deadline. Keep Days 1 to 8. Day 9: mock 1. Day 10: the chapters of Plan A Days 9 and 11, then 42 Security patterns and 45 Decision atlas. Day 11: mock 2. Day 12: the review sheets of Plan A Day 18. Exam on Day 13. About 29 hours.
Dropped (one list): mocks 3 to 5, the repair day, 44 Reference architectures and the rest of Plan A Day 13. The gate is weaker: 70% or more on mock 1 and 75% or more on mock 2 <!-- no-fact: plan -->.

The retake rule, relative: after a failed exam you must wait [14 calendar days](exam-retake-wait) before a retake, so a retake is possible on Day 27 at the earliest. Count back 14 calendar days from your deadline: that is the last day for a first exam that keeps one retake. Each attempt costs the [full registration fee for each exam attempt](exam-retake-attempts-and-fee) of [150 USD](exam-cost).
Choose it only if your Day 1 practice set is 70% or more <!-- no-fact: plan --> and a recorded fail costs you nothing.
Exam trap callout start-here-trap-quick-retake; ends with <!-- trap: start-here-trap-quick-retake -->.

Keep the preview's gate rules unchanged. A 3-column plain table (Gate | If | Then) with the preview's six rows; every cell with a percentage ends with <!-- no-fact: plan -->. Gate 1 after mock 3 (Day 14): mocks 2 and 3 both 80% or more: you are ahead, mock 5 is optional; mock 3 under 65%: move the exam now (Plan B); anything between: continue. Gate 2 after mock 5 (Day 17): your last two mocks both 80% or more: go (your own rule); both 75% or more, no domain under 65% and 10 minutes left: go (the softer rule; a later date leaves no retake either); anything lower: Plan B. Plan C has its own gate on Day 11 (see plan.gates g3).

One sentence: these percentages are the book's own rule for practice sets, not an AWS threshold. The real exam reports a [scaled score of 100–1,000](exam-passing-score) with a passing score of [720](exam-passing-score), and scores are [scaled scores, rather than the raw number of questions scored correct](exam-scaled-scoring). The exam uses a [compensatory scoring model](exam-compensatory-scoring): one weak domain does not fail you by itself, which is why the softer rule allows a domain at 65%.

Timing of a move: you can reschedule [up to 24 hours before](exam-reschedule-window) the exam time, and each appointment can [only be rescheduled twice](exam-reschedule-limit). So decide Gate 2 on the evening of Day 17, and remember that each switch (Plan C to A, or A to B) uses one of the two.

Optional extra measure before Gate 2: the Official Practice Exam on AWS Skill Builder has [the same question style and rigor as the certification exam](exam-official-practice-exam-scaled-score) and gives a [scaled score](exam-official-practice-exam-scaled-score) (subscription; no price, fr-0009 is open). Leave this sentence out if the section runs over 250 words.
Two Exam trap callouts: start-here-trap-720-is-a-percentage and start-here-trap-move-at-the-last-minute, each ending with its trap comment.

contents: One list of the five codes, each code in bold with its meaning from SPEC lint.cause_codes and the repair: **K** did not know: read the subsection that the explanation links. **C** confused two similar things: open the page of 45 Decision atlas for that pair. **W** missed a word in the stem: do ten questions stem-first (cover the options, name the constraint, then read). **T** time: answer, flag, move on, and return at the end. **D** dated question that assumes an old limit: read the chapter's Changed recently entry; on the real exam, [Choose the best available answer from the options in the question](exam-choose-best-available-answer).

One sentence for code D: when a service changes, AWS will [replace exam questions determined to be impacted by the change](exam-changed-service-questions-replaced), and a new feature must be [generally available for 3 months](exam-new-feature-wait) before it appears on an exam; so a D miss usually comes from older practice material, not from the real exam.
One line: review 'sure but wrong' rows first (Sure = yes and the answer was wrong).
One sentence: write one row for each wrong answer and each lucky guess, also from the mocks. Sure is your confidence mark, yes or no.

Exactly one table of kind log, header 'Date | Question | Cause | Sure | Fix', with one example row from CONVENTIONS-2 S1: | Day 3 | sample-q002 | W | yes | Read the last sentence first |. The reader adds the other rows.

gates.text: Gate 1 after mock 3. Mocks 2 and 3 both 80% or more: you are ahead, mock 5 is optional. Mock 3 under 65%: move the exam now and switch to Plan B. Anything between: continue Plan A.
Gate 2 after mock 5, decided this evening. Last two mocks both 80% or more: go. Both 75% or more, no domain under 65% and 10 minutes left: go. Anything lower: move the exam and switch to Plan B.
Plan C gate after mock 2. Mock 1 under 70% or mock 2 under 75%: move the exam to Day 19 and continue with Plan A at Day 13.
Plan C choice. Choose Plan C only if your official practice set is 70% or more and a recorded fail costs you nothing. Otherwise follow Plan A.

traps.belief: You can add ESL +30 later, after you book the exam, and you must request it again for each exam.
traps.truth: ESL +30 is a 30-minute exam extension that only needs to be requested once, before you register, and it applies to all future exam registrations.

traps.belief: A feature that AWS launched last month can be the right answer on your exam.
traps.truth: A new product, service or feature must be generally available for 3 months before it appears on any AWS Certification exam; the book labels such features 'not examinable yet'.

traps.belief: If an early exam fails, you can retake it a few days later at no extra cost.
traps.truth: After a failed exam you must wait 14 calendar days before a retake, and you pay the full registration fee for each exam attempt.

traps.belief: A passing score of 720 means about 72% of the questions right, so a 72% mock means a pass.
traps.truth: 720 is a scaled score on a scale of 100 to 1,000; AWS reports scaled scores rather than the raw number of questions scored correct, so no mock percentage converts to it. The mock thresholds are the book's own rule.

traps.belief: If a gate fails, you can move the exam the day before, as often as you need.
traps.truth: You can reschedule up to 24 hours before the exam time, and each exam appointment can only be rescheduled twice.

Chapter 46 can reuse these ids with trap-ref.
